newsitem.title: JAPAN: US auto industry head says favours 100 yen to dlr.
newsitem.headline: US auto industry head says favours 100 yen to dlr.

text.p: American Automobile Manufacturers Association president Andrew Card said on Wednesday that the dollar should be around 100 yen as a weaker yen hurts the ability of U.S. car makers to compete in the Japanese market.

Card said in a telephone interview with Reuters Financial Television that the dollar at 110 yen could hurt the progress which Japan and the United States have made since last year's car trade pact. The dollar was hovering above 110 yen in morning trade in Tokyo.
"I think the yen-dollar relationship...should be more in the neighbourhood of 100 yen per dollar," he said.
"I think once the yen hits 110 yen per dollar, it puts a tremendous strain on the ability of GM, Ford and Chrysler to meet the expectations of Japanese consumers," he said.

Commenting on a remark by U.S. Commerce Secretary Mickey Kantor that the dollar's recent strength against the yen appears not to have hurt U.S. car sales to Japan, Card said Kantor may have made "a plain mistake".
"He (Kantor) is understanding our challenges... I don't think he really believes that (the statement)," Card said.
"So the 110 (yen) level is, I think, a point where we are saying 'please pay attention'. There is a lot of damage that would come as a result of this exchange rate," he said.
